verdict.rationale: Cloudflare's own docs describe WebSocket media adapters that let a server-side process, such as a Durable Object, receive live call audio as PCM without implementing a WebRTC client and send PCM audio back into the SFU for WebRTC clients to hear. They also document a Workers AI flow that transcribes microphone audio and sends generated speech back to browsers, with a 15-second reconnect retry. missing for 10: independent or hands-on corroboration of the agent round-trip, documented latency figures, and evidence of the agent appearing as a named participant in a RealtimeKit meeting rather than as an SFU adapter endpoint.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, a server-side agent joins a session as a participant that receives live audio and publishes speech back in realtime

citations.quote: Any server that accepts WebSockets, such as a Durable Object, can receive live call audio as PCM samples and video as JPEG frames without implementing a WebRTC client.
You can also send PCM audio into the SFU for WebRTC clients to hear.
Transcribe microphone audio with Workers AI, then send generated speech to browsers through WebSocket media adapters.
For WebRTC-to-WebSocket streaming, the SFU retries the same endpoint for up to 15 seconds after a temporary disconnect.
